prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling remains the clearest case on the shortlist of a general method that changed how chemists build bonds: aryl amines moved from a substrate-limited transformation to a routine one through systematic ligand design by Buchwald and Hartwig, with decades of independent confirmation, and routine use in medicinal chemistry and process routes. Round 1 did not produce a competing candidate with comparable breadth of adoption and a clean two-name attribution. Base editing is the one achievement six of us share, and its chemical content is concrete: a deaminase performs a defined nucleobase transformation at a programmed site, and the adenine editor needed a deaminase evolved to act on DNA. That is a chemical invention, not RNA-guided cleavage, so the 2020 prize is not a bar. A citation naming the conversion of a base answers the chair's wording question. Liu alone for this part keeps the union at three people and names the person who conceived and drove the programme.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection to B054 is still the 2010 prize for Pd cross-coupling, and I have not seen the committee settle whether C-N coupling is a new bond-forming problem or a ligand-driven extension. I think it is new, but I cannot claim consensus. For B018, the Target-AID priority claim of Kondo and Nishida is unresolved for me: I cannot verify dates from the files I am allowed to read, and a Liu-only citation does not cover them. Clinical safety is still accumulating. A two-part prize joining synthetic methodology and chemical biology may also read as assembled rather than unified, and I accept that Linke and Aqvist offer a more thematically tidy pairing (read and write DNA).

responses.point: Chabes argues the trio Liu, Komor and Gaudelli matches the experimental lineage of the cytosine and adenine editors, and that dropping the trainees could look like diluting the work.
responses.response: His point that the adenine editor needed evolved TadA acting on DNA is the reason I regard base editing as chemistry. I still read cytosine and adenine editors as one concept realised twice under one programme, so I would credit Liu alone and note the trainees' role in the scientific background. If the committee decided the adenine editor is a separate inventive step, I would want base editing as a stand-alone prize with his three names, because under the three-person limit that trio cannot sit beside a two-name B054 part. I would take that over dropping Komor and Gaudelli only if the primary record clearly showed it; I have no such evidence.

responses.point: Linke and Aqvist pair Liu with Balasubramanian and Klenerman for sequencing by synthesis, as chemistry for reading and rewriting DNA, and Linke asks what is new after Sanger and how Rothberg and Mayer are handled.
responses.response: The reading-and-writing frame gives the tidier citation, and the reversible-terminator chemistry is real nucleotide chemistry. I still do not move B058 into my configuration. His own questions remain open: what is chemically new compared with Sanger terminator chemistry, and why the 454 lineage and Mayer are excluded. Two DNA-technology parts also leave the committee without a molecule-making achievement. I regard B058 as the best fallback for a second part if B054 fails to get a majority, and I would support it with Balasubramanian and Klenerman only, stating plainly that the platform lineages are not credited.

responses.point: Aqvist treats B054 as a lower alternative and reads the overlap with 2010 more relaxed, while he moved toward a two-part prize with sequencing after hearing the round.
responses.response: I agree with his test of simple in principle plus consequences, and C-N coupling meets it as well as sequencing does. Where we differ is maturity weighting. Cross-coupling has more than thirty years of use and no open safety or clinical questions, whereas base editing, which we both include, is still accumulating evidence. His view that Kosugi is a precursor I share, so the attribution is as clean as his sequencing pair. I would ask him which second part he would accept if sequencing were judged technology rather than chemistry.

responses.point: Zou ranks perovskites first but names Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling or base editing as the safer mature choice if the field is judged too young.
responses.response: Her own case-against is the argument I would press: stability, lead toxicity, crowded credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel, Kanatzidis and Seok, and much device engineering. Her fallback to B054 or B018 describes exactly my configuration, so I hope she can support it on the mature-method ground. I accept the structure-property merit of the perovskite work and the point that it is a materials class reproduced worldwide, but I do not think a three-person cut can be defended today.

responses.point: Aili pairs Liu with Crews and Ciulli for PROTACs, calling induced proximity a molecular design principle, while noting no approved degrader and the omission of Deshaies and the cereblon work.
responses.response: The design principle is attractive and B023 stays my first alternative. Her own reservations decide it for me: the PROTAC and cereblon-glue branches credit different people, a Crews and Ciulli pair omits Deshaies, and no degrader has yet been approved from the core modality. I answer the chair's question on B023 by saying the novelty is the heterobifunctional design, but then a prize invites an attribution dispute I would rather avoid this year.

uncertainties: Whether a majority accepts that C-N coupling is a new chemical problem relative to the 2010 prize.
Dates for Target-AID (Nishida, Kondo) against the Liu laboratory cytosine editor, which I cannot verify from permitted files; if Target-AID clearly preceded, a Liu-only citation weakens.
Whether cytosine and adenine editors count as one achievement or two.
Whether a synthetic-methodology and chemical-biology pairing is judged coherent, or the committee prefers a stand-alone base-editing prize or the B018 plus B058 pairing.
Long-term clinical safety of base editing, which I recall from memory and have not verified.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. My mentor Masamune, my institutions (Chalmers, KTH, Lund, Tartu) and my Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr have no tie to any shortlisted credited name that I know of. I disclose again that I lean toward the synthetic-methodology candidate B054 because it is my own field, and colleagues should weigh that.
